Question: Why did God allow Adam and Eve to sin?
ShortAnswer: God allowed Adam and Eve to sin because He made them with real freedom, and real love requires real choice. He did not cause their sin, but He permitted it — and from the beginning, He had a plan to redeem it through Christ.
DetailedAnswer: This is one of the hardest questions in the Bible, and Scripture does not give us a complete explanation — it gives us truths we hold together. God made Adam and Eve good and gave them one command (Genesis 2:16-17), which means obedience was meaningful precisely because disobedience was possible. Love that cannot choose is not love; it is programming. God warned them plainly, so their choice was informed and free. At the same time, God was not caught off guard: before the foundation of the world, He had chosen a people in Christ (Ephesians 1:4-5), and Revelation speaks of 'the Lamb who was slain from the creation of the world' (Revelation 13:8). God permitted the Fall as part of a larger story in which His grace, mercy, and justice would be displayed more fully than they ever could be in an unfallen world — supremely at the cross, where He took the consequences of human sin upon Himself. Paul ends his own wrestling with God's purposes in wonder: 'Oh, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgments' (Romans 11:33). We may not understand fully, but we can trust the God who brought redemption out of rebellion.
